d: Open-source WordPress SEO toolkit for news publishers.

d: A local editorial checklist for every story. Scores each article on headline, description, content depth, subheadings, featured image, dates and links, then lists the stories to review first. Scoring runs locally, so article text is not sent to an external service. It is a checklist, not a ranking prediction.
w: SEO Score Write and optimize seo score

d: Connected structured data for stories and publisher. Configure publisher identity, article types and media in one place. PublishRank outputs a linked JSON-LD graph with publisher, author, WebSite, WebPage, article, image and breadcrumb entities, with a copyable preview in the editor.
w: Schema Write and optimize schema

d: Show who is behind each story. Keep author details such as role and subject expertise next to your content so bylines and author schema describe real people.
w: Author Expertise Write and optimize author expertise

d: Find link opportunities and orphan pages. Review inbound links and suggested connections across your archive so older stories keep getting readers and crawlers.
w: Internal Links Write and optimize internal links

d: Smaller images, consistent social previews. Review image dimensions and file sizes, then create optimized copies with your chosen width, quality and WebP or JPEG output. The original stays on disk. Optional watermarking for social images is separate.
w: Image Optimizer Write and optimize image optimizer

d: Bulk edits for large archives. Edit selected SEO metadata in bulk, clear chosen fields on purpose, and fill missing image alt text from attachment titles. Existing alt text and edit permissions are respected.
w: Publisher Toolkit Write and optimize publisher toolkit

d: Describe a physical place to search engines. Add local business details for publishers and newsrooms that serve a specific place or have an office readers can visit.
w: Local SEO Write and optimize local seo

d: Content maintenance at a glance. Spot stale, thin or duplicate-looking content and decide what to update, merge or retire.
w: Insights Write and optimize insights

d: Prove ownership without touching files. Paste the meta tag token from Google, Bing, Yandex, Baidu, Naver, Seznam, Pinterest or Meta, or add any other verification tag. Upload a verification file and PublishRank serves it from your site root. Then test exactly what a crawler sees.
w: Site Verification Get discovered site verification

d: Check the XML before search engines do. Inspect your sitemap index and Google News sitemap for valid XML, duplicate URLs, child references and counts. The dashboard gives you both URLs to submit.
w: Sitemap Health Get discovered sitemap health

d: Optional, read-only search reports. Connect Google Search Console to view search reports inside WordPress. Connecting is optional and core features work without it.
w: Search Console Get discovered search console

d: Settings for each engine you submit to. Keep the optional discovery services you use in one screen, from verification to submission settings.
w: Search Engines Get discovered search engines

d: Tell participating engines when you publish. Send new and updated URLs to IndexNow and review the submission log. An accepted response means the endpoint acknowledged the request, not that a page was crawled or indexed.
w: IndexNow Get discovered indexnow

d: Preview and test crawl rules safely. Inspect directives with a live preview and a URL rule tester. Manage sitemap lines and AI crawler presets. Robots.txt guides crawlers; it does not protect private content.
w: Robots.txt Get discovered robots txt

d: A curated map of your site for AI agents. Publish a plain Markdown llms.txt with your site summary, homepage, recent articles, pages and editorial standards, plus an optional extended file. It checks the file for problems and shows a preview. It does not grant or deny crawler access.
w: AI & llms.txt Get discovered ai llms txt

d: Local trends, no visitor tracking. See the editorial score trend, published counts and IndexNow responses over 7, 30 or 90 days, and export the data as CSV. Nothing about visitors or article content goes to a remote analytics service.
w: Analytics Get discovered analytics

d: Allow or block networks and countries. Block IP addresses or CIDR ranges, add trusted exceptions and set country rules through a trusted proxy such as Cloudflare. Administrators, login, REST, feeds, robots.txt, llms.txt and sitemaps are never blocked. Rules run locally and no visitor IP is stored.
w: Traffic Guard Protect and maintain traffic guard

d: Move stories without losing readers. Create exact or regular-expression redirects with 301, 302, 303, 307 and 308 codes or a 410 Gone response, import rules in bulk and check for loops.
w: Redirects Protect and maintain redirects

d: Learn which missing URLs people request. An opt-in log groups requested paths with hit counts and referrers. Turn any entry into a redirect. IP addresses are not stored.
w: 404 Monitor Protect and maintain 404 monitor

d: Audit broken and redirected links. Run an audit for broken internal links, links that pass through redirects and orphan pages, with an optional slower check of external URLs. It uses local analysis and no API.
w: Link Intelligence Protect and maintain link intelligence

d: See what your site actually outputs. Inspect conflicting SEO plugins, theme compatibility, frontend metadata, canonicals, schema and sitemap output when something looks wrong.
w: Diagnostics Protect and maintain diagnostics

d: Know what changed and when. Review earlier configuration changes so you can trace a sudden change in SEO output back to its cause.
w: Configuration History Protect and maintain configuration history

d: Your publishing health in one screen. Shows SEO health checks, published articles, 404 hits, redirect rules and IndexNow status, with the sitemap URLs to submit and a shortcut to every workspace.
w: Dashboard Set up and control dashboard

d: Site-wide defaults for everything. Set titles, metadata, News sitemap options and optional administrator access controls once, then let automatic SEO handle each article.
w: Settings Set up and control settings

d: A guided first-run review. Walk through the essentials in order when you install PublishRank, so a new site starts with sensible defaults.
w: Setup Wizard Set up and control setup wizard

d: Your publisher identity. Manage the account details that tie your installation to your publication.
w: Publisher Account Set up and control publisher account

d: Guides inside WordPress. Open the bundled documentation and troubleshooting steps without leaving the admin.
